title: Depression-era trio jobs at the athletic club and West End bungalow
summary: Bigard recalls working with Walter Decou, Charlie Love and others at the Fifth Ward Athletic Club and a West End bungalow around 1930. Pay was a dollar and a half a night, nine to two.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Mm-hmm. Talking about Walter D. Coo, I believe you said you worked with him way back.
Oh, yeah. I worked with him pretty regular.
No, but way back you said you worked in a trio in the Depression?

Oh, I worked at Captain Petona, Fifth Wall Athletic Club. Yeah. Captain Petona used to own that. Mm-hmm. Who was that? And I worked with him over at West End Bungle for Old Man Albert Duboss. Yeah. And the band over there was Willie Paggio's on Trumpet. Mm-hmm. Old Man Sam Dutre, Sr. was on sax. Mm-hmm. Before then, they had Big Iron Lowry. You might have heard talk about him. Oh, yeah. Well, he was working there, and he got kind of sick, and he left. Mm-hmm. So Old Man Sam Dutre, Sr., he took his place, and Walter and myself. Mm-hmm.
That was in the year of about 1930.

That was at the bungalow? Yeah. Yeah. So when would it be that you were playing at the athletic club? What year would that be? That was during the time of Depression. That was just before that? Depression, yeah. We would get no more than a dollar and a half a nine. That was what you were earning, a dollar and a half? Yeah. A dollar and a half a nine. What was the hours, how long you had to play for? Well, we used to go to work at nine and knock off at two. Oh, yeah, yeah. Nine to two. Who else do you say was in that trio? Charlie Love. Oh, yeah, Charlie Love. Yeah, Charlie Love. Could Charlie read music? Yeah. Charlie read music. Did you play all for music in that little trio? Yeah. And Walter Dink, who also read music. Yeah. But I mean, did they play anything like the blues or anything like that, didn't they?
